newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian shares firm for seventh consecutive day.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian shares firm for seventh consecutive day.

text.p: Slovenia's blue-chip SBI index firmed 0.65 percent on Monday, taking its gains to 7.7 percent over the past seven consecutive trading days.
Market participants forecast the index would clear 1,600 points by the end of the week.

"I expect the index will firm to over 1,600 points by the end of this week and we are looking forward to a very hot autumn when strong gains can be expected," said Alain Al Soufi, a trader of brokerage BPH.

He said he believed international investors had put 30 to 40 million marks ($16.3 million to $21.8 million) in Slovenian shares since the end of June when the Bank of Slovenia eased foreign investment rules.
"I expect foreigners will spend between 50 to 100 million marks for Slovenian securities per month in the autumn," Al Soufi added.

Analysts said most foreign demand was attracted by companies with the largest capitalisation on the market like pharmaceutical makers Lek and Krka, petrol trader Petrol, trading firm Mercator and health resort Terme Catez.
"Strong foreign demand in the past month initiated a winning streak that could last for months with temporary corrections," an analyst said.
The SBI index rose 10.19 points to 1,582.67.
Petrol trader Petrol was most actively traded, up 1.91 percent to 25,050 tolars on volume of 3,073 shares.
"Petrol will most likely rise further on strong foreign demand as petrol and pharmaceutical companies are currently most popular among international investors in general," a trader said.
Financial consultancy Primofin was the top gainer, up 8.47 percent to 10,500 tolars in volume of only four shares.
Construction company GPG was the leading decliner, down 5.17 percent to 5,500 on volume of 500 shares. Traders attributed the fall to poor liquidity of the share.
